message.reasoning:
Let me evaluate the submission against the rubric.

C1: Mission concept and rationale (40% weight, but levels 0-10 scaled). The submission has a clear mission goal, objectives, requirements, users (AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM), rationale with references. Strong. Accomplished, mark 9.

C2: Project plan (30%). Gantt chart, task descriptions, contingencies table, information sources table, software choice (STK) with justification tied to mission. Very robust. Accomplished, mark 9.

C3: Preliminary progress (10%). Hand calcs for orbit, period, inclination, ground track shift, swath; interpretation; STK scenario set up. Good. Accomplished, mark 8.

C4: Presentation (20%). Well structured, headings, figures labelled, references cited in text and match list. Some minor issues: reference [6] cited for BoM SST products but [6] is NOAA "How does climate change affect coral reefs?" — mismatch. Also [10] WWF cited for bleaching severity — okay-ish. Reference [2] National Geographic. Figure 1 is a Gantt chart image. Formatting consistent. Accomplished, mark 8.

Technical issues:
- Inclination 97.8° for 600 km SSO: correct (~97.8°). Good.
- Period 5801 s: check: a=6978 km, T = 2π√(a³/μ) = 2π√(6978³/398600). 6978³ = 3.398e11... let's compute: 6978² = 48,692,484; ×6978 = 3.398e11 (3.3978e11). /398600 = 852,400. sqrt = 923.3. ×2π = 5801 s. Correct.
- Orbits per day 14.9: 86400/5801 = 14.89. Correct.
- Ground track shift: 360° × T/86164 = 360 × 5801/86164 = 24.24°. Correct. But 24.2° at equator = 24.2 × 111.32 = 2694 km ≈ 2700 km. Correct.
- Swath: 10 m × 6000 pixels = 60 km. Correct.
- Interpretation: "reef is up to about 250 km wide" — the GBR is up to ~250 km wide in the south? Actually the GBR Marine Park extends ~230-250 km wide in some parts. Fine.
- Issue: "neighbouring ground tracks are 2,700 km apart on the same day" — correct for consecutive orbits, but over a week the tracks converge; also at 10 m GSD with 60 km swath, weekly coverage of 2300 km length × 250 km width requires ~ (2300/60) × (250/60) ≈ 38 × 4.2 = 160 swaths; with 14.9 orbits/day and ~half in daylight, ~7 usable passes/day → ~23 days. So the conclusion is right. But the statement "weekly coverage not guaranteed" is correct. However, the analysis ignores that ground tracks converge at higher latitudes — GBR is at 10-25°S, so not much convergence. Fine.
- Minor: "Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic" — actually 30% increase in hydrogen ion concentration, commonly stated as "30% more acidic". Acceptable.
- "bathymetry (current satellites have only mapped GBR depths to a resolution of 100 meters per pixel)" — the gbr100 model is 100 m resolution, derived from Landsat; fine.
- Reference [6] mismatch: cited for BoM SST products but is NOAA climate change page. Also BoM is mentioned as user but no BoM reference.
- Reference [4] is a Nature news article, not the primary Asner paper — acceptable but weak.
- Table 3 "Inclination for sun-synchronism ... 97.8°" — no calculation shown, just stated. Minor.
- Gantt chart: weeks 2-10, but "Wk 4 5/10" — dates: 21/9, 28/9, 5/10, 12/10, 19/10, 26/10, 2/11, 9/11, 16/11. Consistent weekly. Good.
- Gantt: "STK Simulations" bar extends to Wk 10 but text says final design and simulation completed by end of week 9 — minor inconsistency. Actually the STK Simulations row is blue through Wk 10. And "Editing & Finalisation" Wk 9-10. Minor.
- Also Gantt shows "Background Research" blue through Wk 8, and "Mission Concept" gold in Wk 2-3 — consistent with "complete as part of preliminary report".
- Contingency: "fall back to the STK demo version, or PIGI after registering for a licence" — good, addresses R3.
- R2: relate plan to space segment, launch and orbits — yes, Launch Specifics, Orbit Specifics, COEs/AOEs.
- R3: software selected: STK. Yes.
- R5: information sources listed. Yes.
- R6: preliminary technical content. Yes.

One technical nit: "Ground-track shift per orbit at the equator 360° × T / 86,164 s" — using sidereal day is correct.

Another: the swath of 60 km at 10 m GSD with 6000 pixels — plausible.

Another potential issue: 600 km SSO at 97.8° — for 600 km, SSO inclination is about 97.8°. Correct.

Also: "the reef is up to about 250 km wide" — GBR width varies; the Marine Park is ~344,400 km² over 2300 km length, average width ~150 km, max ~250 km. Fine.

Also: objective 1 "Image the full length of the reef (about 2,300 km)" — GBR is ~2,300 km. Correct.

Also: "In 2016, a bleaching killed 30 percent of the reef's coral. In 2017, another 20 percent perished" — commonly cited figures (2016: 29% loss of shallow-water corals; 2017: 20%). Fine.

Also: "Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic since the industrial revolution" — commonly stated.

C4: reference [6] cited in text for BoM SST but content mismatch — a citation accuracy issue. Also [9] eAtlas cited in Table 2 but not cited in text body — actually Table 2 is in text, so it's cited. [7] cited in Table 2. [10], [11] cited in Preliminary Progress. All references cited somewhere. Good.

Marking: C1 9/10, C2 9/10, C3 8/10, C4 8/10.

Weighted: 40% × 9 + 30% × 9 + 10% × 8 + 20% × 8 = 3.6+2.7+0.8+1.6 = 8.7/10.

Now produce JSON.

Evidence quotes must be <=25 words, contiguous, exact.

C1 evidence: "Give reef managers direct, repeatable observations of coral colour over the whole Great Barrier Reef, so that bleaching is detected within days" — that's 24 words? Count: Give(1) reef2 managers3 direct4 repeatable5 observations6 of7 coral8 colour9 over10 the11 whole12 Great13 Barrier14 Reef15 so16 that17 bleaching18 is19 detected20 within21 days22. 22 words. Good.

C2 evidence: "The order follows the mission: the imaging requirements (objectives 1 and 2) fix the orbit altitude and local time" — 20 words. Good.

C3 evidence: "the reef is up to about 250 km wide, so a 60 km swath needs at least five neighbouring passes" — 20 words.

C4 evidence: "Figure 1: Project Gantt chart, Weeks 2 to 10 (gold = completed, blue = planned, red lines = report deadlines)." — 19 words.

Requirements: all met.

Technical issues list with where.

Overall <=60 words.
